subject: MATH
title: Algebra II
description: Algebra II extends the function families of Algebra I to polynomial, rational, radical, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions, and introduces complex numbers, sequences and series, and statistical inference. Each unit pairs procedural fluency with modeling tasks drawn from real data, consistent with the 2023 California Mathematics Framework's emphasis on big ideas and data science. Graphing technology (Desmos) is used throughout.
framework: California Common Core State Standards for Mathematics (Algebra II, traditional pathway); 2023 California Mathematics Framework

standards.N-RN.1: Explain how the meaning of rational exponents follows from extending properties of integer exponents.
standards.N-RN.2: Rewrite expressions involving radicals and rational exponents using properties of exponents.

standards.A-SSE.4: Derive the formula for the sum of a finite geometric series and use it to solve problems.
standards.A-APR.1: Understand that polynomials form a system closed under addition, subtraction, and multiplication; perform these operations.
standards.A-APR.2: Know and apply the Remainder Theorem.

standards.A-APR.6: Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms using inspection, long division, or a CAS.

standards.A-CED.1: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems.
standards.A-CED.2: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships; graph them.
standards.A-CED.3: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities and by systems; interpret solutions as viable or nonviable.
standards.A-CED.4: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest.
standards.A-REI.2: Solve simple rational and radical equations in one variable, and explain how extraneous solutions may arise.
standards.A-REI.4b: Solve quadratic equations by inspection, square roots, completing the square, the quadratic formula, and factoring; recognize complex solutions.
standards.A-REI.6: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately, focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.
standards.A-REI.7: Solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation and a quadratic equation algebraically and graphically.
standards.A-REI.11: Explain why x-coordinates of intersection points of y = f(x) and y = g(x) are solutions of f(x) = g(x); find them approximately using technology.
standards.F-IF.4: Interpret key features of graphs and tables of functions in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features.
standards.F-IF.6: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function over a specified interval.
standards.F-IF.7b: Graph square root, cube root, and piecewise-defined functions, including step and absolute value functions.
standards.F-IF.7c: Graph polynomial functions, identifying zeros when suitable factorizations are available and showing end behavior.
standards.F-IF.7e: Graph exponential and logarithmic functions, showing intercepts and end behavior, and trigonometric functions showing period, midline, and amplitude.
standards.F-IF.8: Write a function defined by an expression in different but equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties.
standards.F-IF.9: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way.
standards.F-BF.1b: Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations.
standards.F-BF.2: Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and with an explicit formula, and use them to model situations.
standards.F-BF.3: Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x)+k, k f(x), f(kx), and f(x+k); find k from graphs.
standards.F-BF.4a: Solve an equation of the form f(x) = c for a simple invertible function and write an expression for the inverse.
standards.F-LE.2: Construct linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences, given a graph, description, or table.
standards.F-LE.4: For exponential models, express as a logarithm the solution to ab^(ct) = d and evaluate the logarithm using technology.
standards.F-LE.4.2: (CA) Use the definition of logarithms to translate between logarithms in any base.
standards.F-LE.4.3: (CA) Understand and use the properties of logarithms to simplify logarithmic numeric expressions and to identify their approximate values.
standards.F-LE.5: Interpret the parameters in a linear or exponential function in terms of a context.
standards.F-TF.1: Understand radian measure of an angle as the length of the arc on the unit circle subtended by the angle.
standards.F-TF.2: Explain how the unit circle in the coordinate plane enables the extension of trigonometric functions to all real numbers.
standards.F-TF.2.1: (CA) Graph all six basic trigonometric functions.
standards.F-TF.5: Choose trigonometric functions to model periodic phenomena with specified amplitude, frequency, and midline.
standards.F-TF.8: Prove the Pythagorean identity sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 and use it to find trig values given one value and the quadrant.
standards.S-ID.4: Use the mean and standard deviation of a data set to fit it to a normal distribution and estimate population percentages.
standards.S-IC.1: Understand statistics as a process for making inferences about population parameters based on a random sample.
standards.S-IC.2: Decide if a specified model is consistent with results from a given data-generating process, e.g., using simulation.

standards.S-IC.4: Use data from a sample survey to estimate a population mean or proportion; develop a margin of error through simulation.
standards.S-IC.5: Use data from a randomized experiment to compare two treatments; use simulations to decide if differences are significant.
standards.S-MD.6: (+) Use probabilities to make fair decisions (e.g., drawing by lots, using a random number generator).
standards.S-MD.7: (+) Analyze decisions and strategies using probability concepts.

units.title: Functions, Transformations, and Systems
units.big_idea: Every function family can be moved and stretched the same ways, and systems model competing constraints.

units.title: Quadratic Functions and Complex Numbers
units.big_idea: Quadratics can be written in forms that reveal different features, and complex numbers complete their solutions.

units.title: Polynomial Functions
units.big_idea: Polynomials behave like integers: they can be factored, divided, and their zeros determine their graphs.

units.title: Rational Expressions and Functions
units.big_idea: Rational functions are quotients of polynomials whose restrictions create asymptotes and holes.

units.title: Radical Functions, Rational Exponents, and Inverses
units.big_idea: Radicals and rational exponents are two notations for the same idea, and inverses undo functions.

units.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
units.big_idea: Exponential functions model constant-percent change, and logarithms are the tool to solve for the exponent.

units.title: Trigonometric Functions
units.big_idea: The unit circle extends trigonometry to all real numbers and lets us model periodic phenomena.

units.title: Sequences and Series
units.big_idea: Patterns of repeated addition or multiplication can be written recursively, explicitly, and summed.

units.title: Statistics and Inference
units.big_idea: Randomization and variability let us draw conclusions about populations and treatments from samples.

units.title: Modeling Capstone and Final Exam
units.big_idea: Choosing the right function family is the heart of mathematical modeling.

objectives: Select and justify a function model for real data
materials: public data set (CA population, COVID, temperature)

days.title: Choose data
days.work: Choose a real data set and graph it.

days.title: Model fitting
days.work: Fit linear, quadratic, exponential, and sinusoidal models; compare residuals.

days.title: Justification
days.work: Write a justification for the best model, including limitations.

days.title: Presentation
days.work: Prepare a 5-minute presentation of the model and predictions.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present the capstone and answer questions.

days.title: Review: Units 1–5
days.work: Mixed review on quadratics, polynomials, rationals, and radicals.

days.title: Review: Units 6–9
days.work: Mixed review on exponentials, logs, trig, sequences, and statistics.

days.title: Final exam part 1
days.work: Non-calculator section.

days.title: Final exam part 2
days.work: Calculator section with modeling tasks.

days.title: Reflection
days.work: Review exam errors and write a reflection on growth and readiness for Precalculus.
